brandStory.heroEyebrow: ブランド物語 · Brand Story
brandStory.heroBody: This dish holds all our love for Vietnam and the flavors carved deep into our hearts. We bring Vietnam's time-honored hospitality to Japan through traditional recipes.
brandStory.originP1: In 2018, when we moved to Tokyo, we realized something: authentic Vietnamese restaurants were rare in Japan. On occasional business trips to North America we enjoyed great Vietnamese food on the spot — but in Japan there was almost no place worthy of the name.
brandStory.originP2Pre: As Vietnamese living in Japan, we could never forget the flavors we grew up with. Every time we ate out, we searched for the traditional Vietnamese dishes familiar to us since childhood. Above all,
brandStory.originP2Post: — the signature of Vietnamese cuisine, eaten at breakfast, lunch, or dinner — always lingered in our hearts.
brandStory.originP3Pre: Of course there were a few places selling phở in Tokyo. But most were
brandStory.originP3Post: , far removed from the traditional Vietnamese bowl we knew.
brandStory.doubtsTitle: Why has no one done it?
brandStory.doubtsIntro: When we shared the idea, we heard the same three things again and again from friends, colleagues, and people in the industry:
doubts: Phở just doesn't suit the Japanese palate.
Phở hasn't taken root in Japanese eating habits.
Starting a business with this dish would be very hard.
brandStory.beliefTitle: If so, then we should do it ourselves.
brandStory.beliefP1: There were plenty of reasons why hardly anyone opens a real phở shop in Japan. But the founders — who grew up in Vietnam and traveled through many countries — still believed one simple thing:
brandStory.beliefQuote: "Traditional Vietnamese phở is a dish that transcends borders."
brandStory.beliefP2Highlight: "Then we ourselves should be the ones to do it."
brandStory.barrierP1: Making phở sounds simple but is anything but easy. Where to source ingredients rarely circulated in Japan? How much time and labor to recreate the traditional recipe? So many questions.
brandStory.barrierP2Pre: Above all, the most important ingredient is
brandStory.barrierP2Post: . In Vietnam phở is an everyday dish, so finding a maker of fresh noodles is easy. In Japan there is no such workshop. A circular logic:
brandStory.barrierQuoteL1: "Because there is no fresh phở noodle maker, no one uses fresh phở noodles.
brandStory.barrierQuoteL2: Because there is no demand for fresh phở noodles, even if you made them, they wouldn't sell."
brandStory.openingTitle: And then, fresh phở noodles appeared.
brandStory.openingP1: In that context, in 2021, we happened to meet someone willing to make fresh phở noodles for us. At the same time, a broth recipe reproducible in Japan was also complete. Perfect timing.
brandStory.openingP2Pre: Right in the middle of COVID, we still decided to open
brandStory.openingP2Post: is a Vietnamese eatery founded in Japan, devoted to recreating authentic flavors and serving guests with care.
brandStory.ctaEyebrow: こだわり · Attention to detail
brandStory.ctaBody: Broth simmered for 14 hours, seasoning from vegetables, fresh phở noodles every day — three principles that close the story and open a real experience in every bowl.

conceptStory.heroEyebrow: こだわり · Attention to detail
conceptStory.heroBody: A complete bowl of phở holds more than ten hours of effort. We believe true flavor comes from the seemingly smallest things — from how we wash the bones and choose the vegetables to the fresh phở noodles made each day.
conceptStory.phoBoTitleL2: more than ten hours of care.
conceptStory.phoBoIntro: Three steps — one belief: true flavor never comes from haste.

steps.label: Traditional recipe
steps.title: Simmering bones 10–14 hours in a large pot
steps.body: Beef, pork, and chicken bones are washed clean and blanched in boiling water. Each kind of bone has a different firmness, flavor, and aroma — we calculate the right ratio and timing for adding them to the pot to draw out the best of each. The simmer lasts 10 to 14 hours, long enough for sweetness and aroma to dissolve into the broth.

steps.label: Nature's bounty
steps.title: Seasoning from fresh vegetables, minimal MSG
steps.body: Broth from bones is already rich in nutrients, but at Bet屋 we go a step further: we add daikon, sweet corn, and seasonal mushrooms and simmer about 3 more hours for a vegetable broth that warms both body and spirit. We minimize artificial flavor enhancers and favor naturally sourced ingredients.

steps.label: Fresh phở noodles
steps.title: Recreating native flavor with fresh phở noodles
steps.body: Most great phở shops in Vietnam use fresh noodles — they lift the taste and aroma of the broth. But fresh noodles are soft and break easily when cooked, so the cook needs more skill and a finer process than with dried noodles. Fresh phở noodles absorb the broth like grains of rice, so its taste and aroma soak into every strand.

conceptStory.step3Quote: "Fresh phở noodles drink in the broth like grains of rice — every strand carries the full flavor of the pot."
conceptStory.phoGaP1: Compared with beef phở, chicken phở is lighter — but that doesn't mean bland. We extract the best of the chicken to keep its original flavor. The chicken is blanched in boiling water, rinsed immediately in cold water, then simmered gently from cold water for a long time.
conceptStory.phoGaP2Pre: Throughout the simmer, we keep skimming the foam and add lightly seared scallions and ginger — the secret to a broth that is
conceptStory.phoGaP2Post: . The seasoning is only the sweetness of seared onion and root vegetables, combined with Vietnamese fish sauce. Finally, kaffir lime leaf and cinnamon add aroma.
conceptStory.phoGaQuote: "In Vietnam, when sick or tired, people eat phở. A gentle bowl of chicken phở suits even the most off days."

partyStory.heroEyebrow: ケータリング · Parties & Events
partyStory.heroTitle:
A journey through
Vietnam at home.
partyStory.heroBody: A Vietnamese feast for your company, family, or friends — we bring the flavors of Hanoi right to your door. Order per person, customize a combo, or bento boxes for special occasions.
partyStory.introBody: From a simple company lunch to an important celebration — choose what fits your group best.

offerings.title: Party-size servings
offerings.tagline: The more, the more you save
offerings.body: Servings for 5, 10, or 20 people — ready-packed combos of phở, bún, fresh spring rolls, and fried spring rolls. The per-portion price drops with quantity. Perfect for company team meetings, office parties, and family gatherings.

offerings.title: Mix and match your way
offerings.body: Don't like fixed combos? Choose your own counts of beef phở, chicken phở, bún bò Huế, fresh spring rolls, bánh mì, and fried spring rolls — we adjust portions, spice level, and vegetarian / no-onion / gluten-free servings on request.

offerings.title: Special bento boxes
offerings.body: Individual bento for anniversaries, birthdays, parent meetings, and small weddings — packed in wooden or premium cardboard boxes, with optional logo / thank-you card printing. Quantity to order; please book at least 3 days in advance.

partyStory.processTitle: Three steps — from contact to the feast.

steps.title: Get in touch
steps.body: Fill out the form or call directly — tell us the number of people, the pickup date, the location, and the occasion.

steps.title: Menu consultation
steps.body: Our head chef suggests a menu, adjusts for vegetarian / non-spicy / allergy needs, and confirms the final price within 24 hours.

steps.title: Delivery & service
steps.body: Delivered within Tokyo's 23 wards, handed over in person, with boxes/trays collected after the event — clean and on time.

partyStory.contactBody: Call directly, message us on LINE, or send an email — we reply within 24 hours, even on weekends.
